HeroName: Hugues XII de Lusignan, Count of La Marche and Angoulême
Description: Hugues XII de Lusignan is the head of the storied House of Lusignan, ruling as Count of La Marche and Count of Angoulême across the heart of Poitou. At forty-seven, he commands vast territories, dozens of stone fortresses, and thousands of feudal knights, wielding massive political leverage between Paris and English Aquitaine. Carrying the immense aristocratic pride of his ancestors who reigned as Kings of Jerusalem and Cyprus, Hugues consolidated his western dominance by marrying Jeanne de Fougères, absorbing her colossal granite marchland fortress into his domain. An expert in combined-arms warfare and regional diplomacy, he ruled with seasoned gravitas and baronial firmness. Chronicles record that answering the pious call of Saint Louis, Hugues would embark upon the Eighth Crusade in 1270, dying heroically of camp fever before the walls of Tunis. He stands as a towering pillar of French chivalry. At Angoulême, Count Hugues constructed stone cavalry stables and siege-artillery magazines, connecting his vast domains with paved signal avenues stretching to the Atlantic shore. Authoritative, honorable, and universally respected, his rulings at baronial assemblies carried absolute finality, anchoring French royal authority across Poitou. His profound devotion to knightly vows and masterly fortification works have transformed Poitou into an impenetrable sanctuary of righteous chivalry and baronial authority.
Motivations: Consolidate governance across La Marche, Angoulême, and Fougères to expand dynastic power.
Navigate Anglo-French rivalries to protect the historic baronial liberties of Lusignan.
Values: Inviolate dynastic supremacy and territorial integrity of the House of Lusignan.
Devout crusader vows coupled with generous patronage of holy monastic sanctuaries.
Fears: Royal French bailiffs dismantling the ancient private jurisdictions of Poitou.
Perishing abroad on crusade and leaving young heirs exposed to predatory rivals.
SpeechStyle: Speaks with gravelly aristocratic authority and deep baronial resonance, his French dignified, measured, and weighted with the sovereign pride of the Lusignan line.
